title: Origin of the earth and the solar system
competency: Discuss how the Earth and the other members of the solar system formed and changed to their present state.

keywords.def: The Sun and everything that travels around it: planets, dwarf planets, asteroids and meteoroids.
A huge cloud of hot, swirling gas and dust. The solar system formed from one.
The star at the centre of the solar system. Its pull holds the system together; it gives heat and light.
A large body that travels around the Sun on its own orbit. From the Greek planetai, 'wanderers'.
The oval path a planet or other body follows around the Sun.
One of the four planets nearest the Sun (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars): small, solid and rocky.
One of the four planets farthest from the Sun (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune): large and mostly gas.
Another name for an inner planet: solid with a rocky surface, like Earth.
Another name for an outer planet: very large and made mostly of gases.
A planet-like body that is not counted as a full planet, such as Pluto, Ceres and Eris.
A fairly small rocky body that orbits the Sun, mostly between Mars and Jupiter.
A small piece broken off an asteroid.
A meteoroid burning in our atmosphere, seen as a streak of light or 'shooting star'.
A piece of a meteoroid that survives the trip through the air and lands on Earth.
A group of stars that forms a pattern in the night sky. There are 88.

en.text: The Sun, the planets and the small bodies formed from one huge cloud of hot, swirling gas and dust. Gravity pulled the cloud into a spinning disc. The disc split into rings. The centre became the Sun and the outer rings became the planets. Earth formed about 4.6 billion years ago.

am.text: ፀሐይ፣ ፕላኔቶችና ትናንሽ አካላት የተፈጠሩት ከአንድ ግዙፍ የሚሽከረከር የጋዝና የአቧራ ደመና ነው። የስበት ኃይል ደመናውን ወደ ሚሽከረከር ዲስክ ሰበሰበው። ዲስኩ ወደ ቀለበቶች ተከፈለ። መሃሉ ፀሐይ ሆነ፤ የውጭዎቹ ቀለበቶች ፕላኔቶች ሆኑ። ምድር የተፈጠረችው ከ4.6 ቢሊዮን ዓመታት በፊት ገደማ ነው።

screens.title: Where did the Earth come from?
screens.text: Look up at the night sky over Addis Ababa. The Sun, the Moon and the planets all seem very different.
screens.ask: What do you think the Sun and the planets formed from?
opts: One huge cloud of gas and dust
screens.after: Read part A to see what scientists think.

screens.title: A. The origin of the Earth
paras: The Earth's beginning is tied to the beginning of the whole solar system.
Many scientists think the Sun, the planets and the smaller bodies all formed from one huge cloud. The cloud was made of hot, swirling gas and dust. It was mostly hydrogen and helium.
Slowly, gravity pulled the gas and dust together into a thin, spinning disc. Over time the disc split into rings that kept spinning.
The rings at the centre formed the Sun. The outer rings formed the eight planets, including Earth. Geologists estimate the Earth formed about 4.6 billion years ago.
screens.note: Correction: the printed book says "a large flammable of hot swirling gases". The intended word is cloud (scientists call it a nebula).

screens.title: Name it
defs: Nebula
A huge cloud of hot, swirling gas and dust. Our solar system formed from one.
Solar system
The Sun and everything that travels around it.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.text: What did the Sun and the planets form from?
opts: A huge spinning cloud of gas and dust
screens.ans: A huge spinning cloud of gas and dust
screens.why: Gravity pulled the cloud into a disc. The centre became the Sun and the rings became planets.
screens.clue: Read part A again: what was there before the disc?

screens.title: Four stages of formation
screens.text: Follow the solar system from cloud to today.
steps: 1. Cloud: a huge cloud of hot, swirling gas (mostly hydrogen and helium) and dust.
2. Disc: gravity pulls the gas and dust together into a thin, spinning disc.
3. Rings: the disc splits into rings that keep spinning.
4. Today: the centre becomes the Sun; the outer rings become the planets.

screens.title: Put the stages in order
screens.text: Put the stages in order, from first to last.
items: A cloud of gas and dust
screens.why: The cloud pulled into a disc, the disc split into rings, and the rings became the Sun and planets.
screens.clue: What came before the disc? What did the disc split into?

screens.title: How old is the Earth?
screens.ask: Geologists estimate the Earth formed about ___ billion years ago.
screens.why: The Earth is about 4.6 billion years old.
screens.clue: The number is between 4 and 5. Look at the last paragraph of part A.
screens.worked: Part A says the Earth formed about 4.6 billion years ago. So the answer is 4.6.

screens.title: Hana explains to her brother
screens.text: Hana tells her little brother how the Sun formed. Which sentence should she use?
opts: The Sun formed from the centre of the spinning rings.
The Sun formed from the outer rings.
The Sun broke off from the Earth.
The Sun formed after the planets, from their dust.
screens.ans: The Sun formed from the centre of the spinning rings.
screens.why: The rings at the centre formed the Sun. The outer rings formed the planets.
screens.clue: Which rings made the planets? The Sun came from the other part.

en.text: The Sun is a star at the centre of the solar system. It is about 150 million km away. Eight planets travel around it on oval paths called orbits. Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are small rocky inner planets. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are large outer gas giants. Pluto is now a dwarf planet.

am.text: ፀሐይ በሥርዓተ ፀሐይ መሃል ያለች ኮከብ ናት። ከምድር 150 ሚሊዮን ኪሎ ሜትር ገደማ ትርቃለች። ስምንት ፕላኔቶች ምህዋር በሚባሉ ሞላላ መንገዶች ይዞሯታል። ሜርኩሪ፣ ቬነስ፣ ምድርና ማርስ ትናንሽ ድንጋያማ የውስጥ ፕላኔቶች ናቸው። ጁፒተር፣ ሳተርን፣ ዩራነስና ኔፕቱን ግዙፍ የጋዝ የውጭ ፕላኔቶች ናቸው። ፕሉቶ አሁን ድንክ ፕላኔት ናት።

screens.title: Old sunlight?
screens.text: Sunrise lights up the hills around Gondar. That light did not leave the Sun just now.
screens.ask: How long ago do you think the light left the Sun?
screens.after: Read on. You will work it out yourself.

screens.title: B. Members of the solar system
paras: Our solar system is made of one star, eight planets and countless smaller bodies. These include dwarf planets, asteroids and meteoroids.

screens.title: I. The Sun
paras: The Sun is the centre of the solar system. It is huge and made of extremely hot gases.
Its pull holds the whole system together. It is the main source of heat and light.
We do not feel its full heat. Although it is our nearest star, it is about 150 million km away.
screens.note: Focus: The Sun is a star, just like the stars you see at night. It is the largest object in the solar system and holds 99.8% of the system's mass.

screens.title: II. Planets
paras: The word "planet" comes from the Greek word planetai, which means "wanderers".
There are eight planets. All of them travel around the Sun on paths called orbits. Orbits are oval (elliptical) in shape.

Inner planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are closest to the Sun. They are solid, with rocky surfaces. Astronomers call them the terrestrial planets. They are small compared with the outer planets.
Outer planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are farthest from the Sun. They are much larger and made mostly of gases. So they are called gas giants.
screens.note: Figure 1.1: the asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Planet
A large body that travels around the Sun on its own orbit.
Orbit
The oval path a planet follows around the Sun.
Inner planet
Mercury, Venus, Earth or Mars: small, solid and rocky. Also called terrestrial planets.
Outer planet
Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus or Neptune: large and mostly gas. Also called gas giants.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.text: Which group are Jupiter and Saturn in?
screens.why: They are among the four farthest planets and are made mostly of gas.
screens.clue: Find Jupiter in the table. Is it near the Sun or far?

screens.title: How long does sunlight take?
screens.text: The Earth is about 150 million km from the Sun. Light travels about 300,000 km every second.
steps: The sunlight you see left the Sun over 8 minutes ago.

screens.title: Dwarf planets
paras: Until August 2006 Pluto was counted as a planet.
That year the International Astronomical Union made a decision. Pluto, Ceres and Eris should be called dwarf planets. Eris was first called 2003 UB313.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Dwarf planet
A planet-like body not counted as a full planet, such as Pluto, Ceres and Eris.

screens.title: Pluto today
screens.why: In 2006 Pluto, Ceres and Eris were grouped as dwarf planets.
screens.clue: Think about what happened in August 2006.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: The outer planets are small and rocky.
screens.why: The outer planets are large and mostly gas: the gas giants.
screens.clue: Compare what the book says about the inner planets and the outer planets.

screens.title: Sunlight at sunrise
screens.text: Dawit watches sunrise in Gondar at 6:00 a.m. Light takes 500 seconds to arrive from the Sun.
screens.clue: One minute has 60 seconds. How many seconds are in 8 minutes?

screens.title: Why "terrestrial"?
screens.text: The inner planets are called "terrestrial" because they:
opts: Have solid, rocky surfaces like Earth
screens.ans: Have solid, rocky surfaces like Earth
screens.why: Terrestrial means Earth-like: solid and rocky.
screens.clue: What are the inner planets made of?

en.text: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the Sun, mostly between Mars and Jupiter. When asteroids crash, broken pieces are meteoroids. A meteoroid burning in our air is a meteor, or shooting star. A piece that lands is a meteorite. Patterns of stars are constellations; three are named after Ethiopian royalty.

am.text: አስትሮይድ ፀሐይን የሚዞር ትንሽ ድንጋያማ አካል ነው፤ አብዛኞቹ በማርስና በጁፒተር መካከል ናቸው። አስትሮይዶች ሲጋጩ የሚሰበሩት ቁርጥራጮች ሜቲዮሮይድ ይባላሉ። በአየራችን ውስጥ የሚቃጠል ሜቲዮሮይድ ተወርዋሪ ኮከብ ነው። መሬት ላይ የሚወድቀው ቁራጭ ሜቲዮራይት ይባላል። የከዋክብት ቅርጾች ኅብረ ከዋክብት ይባላሉ፤ ሦስቱ በኢትዮጵያ ነገሥታት ስም ተሰይመዋል።

screens.title: A light in the sky
screens.text: One night in Lalibela, a bright streak of light shoots across the sky. It lasts only a second.
screens.ask: What do you think it was?
opts: A piece of rock burning in our air
screens.after: Read on. One piece of rock can have four names.

screens.title: III. Asteroids and IV. Meteoroids
paras: Besides the Sun and planets, many small bodies move around the Sun.
An asteroid is a fairly small rocky body that orbits the Sun. Most are in the main asteroid belt. The belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

screens.title: One piece of rock, four names
steps: Asteroid: a small rocky body orbiting the Sun. Sometimes two asteroids crash into each other.
Meteoroid: the crash breaks off small pieces. These broken pieces are meteoroids.
Meteor: a meteoroid enters our atmosphere and burns. It makes a streak of light, a "shooting star".
Meteorite: part of it survives the trip and lands on Earth.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Asteroid
A fairly small rocky body that orbits the Sun, mostly between Mars and Jupiter.
Meteoroid
A small piece broken off an asteroid.
Meteor
A meteoroid burning in our atmosphere: a "shooting star".
Meteorite
A piece that survives and lands on Earth.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.why: A meteor is a meteoroid burning in our atmosphere. If a piece lands, it becomes a meteorite.
screens.clue: Did it land, or did it burn in the sky?

screens.title: Interesting fact: constellations
paras: Groups of stars that form patterns in the night sky are called constellations. There are 88 of them.
Three are named after Ethiopian royalty in Greek myth.

screens.title: Things to do: stars in the daytime
paras: You need a torch, plain paper, a pencil and a needle.
Draw a circle on the paper around the front of the torch. Make many small holes inside the circle with the needle.
Fix the paper over the torch glass with a rubber band. Keep the switch clear.
In a dark room, shine the torch on a wall. You will see many dots of light, like stars.
Now switch on all the room lights. The dots almost disappear. Compare this with the stars when the Sun rises. Write a short report and present it to the class.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Constellation
A group of stars that forms a pattern in the night sky.

screens.title: Four names
screens.text: Match each name to what it is.
pairs: Small rocky body orbiting the Sun
Streak of light as a rock burns in our air
Rock from space that lands on Earth
screens.why: One piece of rock can be all four, as it travels.
screens.clue: Follow the rock: crash, burn, land.

screens.title: Stars in the daytime
screens.text: Why can't we see stars in the daytime?
opts: Stars switch off in the day
The Sun's light is far brighter than the stars
Stars move to the other side of the Earth
screens.ans: The Sun's light is far brighter than the stars
screens.why: The stars are still there. Sunlight drowns them out, like the torch dots when the room lights go on.

screens.title: Queen of Ethiopia
screens.text: Meron finds a W-shaped constellation in a star map. Its Latin name means "Queen of Ethiopia".
screens.why: Cassiopeia means Queen of Ethiopia. Andromeda is the princess and Cepheus is the king.
screens.clue: Look at the constellation table. Find the queen.
screens.worked: The table lists Andromeda (princess), Cassiopeia (queen) and Cepheus (king). The queen is Cassiopeia.

opts: The Sun and everything that orbits it
All the stars in the night sky
items.ans: The Sun and everything that orbits it
items.why: It is the Sun plus eight planets, dwarf planets, asteroids, meteoroids and other small bodies.
items.clue: Remember that "solar" means of the Sun.

items.text: 2. Which list shows the planets in order from the Sun?
opts: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus
Earth, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
items.ans: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
items.why: The four inner planets come first, then the four gas giants.
items.clue: Which planet is nearest the Sun? Start there.

items.text: 3. Which planet is nearest to the Sun?
items.why: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun.
items.clue: Look at the first row of the planet table.

test.ask: The oval paths that planets follow around the Sun are called ___.
test.why: Planets travel around the Sun on elliptical orbits.

test.text: Which of these is NOT a member of our solar system?
test.why: Constellations are patterns of distant stars, far outside our solar system.

test.text: The Earth formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a cloud of gas and dust.
test.why: Gravity pulled the cloud into a disc and rings; the Earth formed about 4.6 billion years ago.
